issues.legal_issue: A registered lease covenant requiring a tenant to remove a building and surrender the land at the end of the tenancy does not prevent the tenant from claiming the statutory right to purchase the land.
material_facts: The land was leased before tenant-protection rules were extended to the locality, and the tenant constructed a building after the lease began.
The registered lease required the tenant to demolish the building and surrender vacant possession when the tenancy ended.
The landlord sued to recover possession, and the tenant sought to purchase the land under the tenant-protection scheme.
issues.conclusion: The covenant to demolish the building and surrender the land was not a stipulation as to the erection of buildings within the exception in section 12. It therefore did not displace the tenant’s right to seek purchase of the land under section 9.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 9 and 12 of the Madras City Tenants’ Protection Act, 1922, read with its preamble, protect tenants’ statutory rights against contractual limitations. The exception in section 12 for registered written stipulations as to the erection of buildings is strictly construed and covers stipulations concerning matters such as a building’s size, nature, materials, or use, not a covenant to remove it and vacate the land. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.ejectment_proceeding_with_tenant_purchas: A landlord brought a proceeding to recover leased land, and the tenant sought to purchase it under a tenant-protection scheme.
predicates.lease_predated_local_protection: The tenancy began before tenant-protection rules were extended to the locality.
predicates.tenant_built_after_lease: The tenant constructed a building on the leased land after the lease began.
predicates.registered_lease_required_demolition_at_: The tenant agreed in a registered lease to demolish the building and surrender the land when the tenancy ended.

issues.definition: When a tenant seeks to purchase land in an ejectment proceeding and the tenant built after the lease began, a registered covenant to demolish the building and surrender the land at termination does not prevent that claim where the lease predates the local protection rules.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory restriction allowing a tenant to purchase leased land in place of the landlord’s recovery of possession is not an unreasonable restriction on the landlord’s property rights when it serves the public interest in protecting tenants and preserving existing buildings.
material_facts: The tenancy began before tenant-protection rules were extended to the locality, and the tenant had constructed a building on the leased land.
The landlord sought possession after the tenancy ended, although the tenant-protection scheme allowed the tenant to seek purchase of the land.
The scheme applied to a limited class of earlier tenancies and could preserve existing buildings for the purposes for which the land had been leased.

The tenant offered to pay the land’s market value as of the date of the purchase order; the Court therefore did not decide the validity of the statutory price measure based on the lowest market value during an earlier period.
issues.conclusion: The purchase provision did not impose an unreasonable restriction on the landlord’s property rights under Article 19(1)(f). No independent infringement of Article 31(1) could be established. The Court expressed no opinion on the validity of the statutory price measure that it did not need to consider.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9 of the Madras City Tenants’ Protection Act, 1922, was regarded as serving the general public by giving effect to the understanding inducing tenants to build and by conserving building materials through maintaining existing buildings for their leased purposes. The restriction on a landlord’s right to recover possession was therefore not unreasonable under Article 19(1)(f) of the Constitution; absent invalidity under that provision, no independent infringement of Article 31(1) arose. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_tenant_purch: A landlord challenged a scheme that allowed a tenant to purchase leased land instead of the landlord recovering possession.
predicates.lease_predated_local_protection: The tenancy began before tenant-protection rules were extended to the locality.
predicates.tenant_built_on_leased_land: The tenant constructed a building on the leased land.
predicates.existing_buildings_could_be_preserved_fo: The existing tenant-built buildings could be maintained for the purposes for which the land had been leased.

issues.definition: A purchase scheme is not an unreasonable property-right restriction when it is challenged by a landlord in a qualifying earlier tenancy in which the tenant built on the land and the buildings could be preserved for their leased purposes.
